bug_semantics: SitemapLoader.parse_sitemap in libs/community/langchain_community/document_loaders/sitemap.py applies the documented restrict_to_same_domain control only inside the loop over soup.find_all("url") leaf entries (loc_text compared via _extract_scheme_and_domain against self.web_path), but the separate loop over soup.find_all("sitemap") — sitemap-index entries — passes the child <loc> text straight to self.scrape_all([loc.text], "xml")[0] and recurses with els.extend(self.parse_sitemap(soup_child, depth=depth+1)), with no domain comparison and no check for private/loopback/link-local destinations. The recursive fetch reaches WebBaseLoader.scrape_all and an aiohttp GET of an attacker-chosen URL. An attacker who controls or influences an ingested sitemap can therefore point a nested sitemap-index entry at an internal address and make the deploying server fetch it even when the application set restrict_to_same_domain=True specifically to confine outbound requests; because the fetched child sitemap's loc entries are appended into els and later scraped/returned as Documents, internal response content is disclosed to the caller, not merely requested (SSRF with disclosure, CWE-918).
flaw_origin: Commit 7e79f8c136452cbde767ea9a80e4a4caed23fd16 ("Support recursive sitemaps in SitemapLoader (#3146)", 2023-04-22, author Johann-Peter Hartmann <hartmann@mayflower.de>, committer GitHub squash-merge; parent 215dcc2d26679c84b6daacde5d4ebd466f7c30c5) first wrote the vulnerable nested-sitemap mechanism in langchain/document_loaders/sitemap.py: it appended the loop `for sitemap in soup.find_all("sitemap"): ... soup_child = self.scrape_all([loc.text], "xml")[0]; els.extend(self.parse_sitemap(soup_child))` (+7 lines, verified in the diff). The advisory's named sink — the nested sitemap element's loc text fed to scrape_all without the domain restriction — is born here. The later restrict_to_same_domain control introduced by 90e9ec6962dcb9bb6500007d95a11f6b2aee877c (2023-10-17, "Sitemap specify default filter url (#11925)") was applied only to the pre-existing leaf url loop and never extended to this recursive loop, so the first-write of the sink is the recursive-sitemap commit; the code was carried verbatim through libs/integrations (310e9461, 2023-12-03), the langchain-community split (2d18c65f/ed58eeb9, 2023-12-11), the CVE-2024-2965 max_depth patch (9a877c7a, 2024-06-14, which added only a depth cap), and the repo split (9ff5b5d2, 2025-04-29) — all carrier commits of the unchanged sink line.

Earlier partial remediation is not this fix: 9a877c7adbd06f90a2518152f65b562bd90487cc / 73c42306745b0831aa6fe7fe4eeb70d2c2d87a82 (2024-06-14, 'SitemapLoader restrict depth of parsing sitemap (CVE-2024-2965) (#22903)') added only a max_depth=10 recursion cap; after it the nested loop still calls `self.scrape_all([loc.text], "xml")[0]` with no domain check (verified in the diff hunk and at 7ecdac52:libs/community/.../sitemap.py:199) — evidence-only, not a fix for CVE-2026-72848.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory (GHSA-vg8m-4p2q-gcjh / CVE-2026-72848, published 2026-08-21, NVD-sourced, Unreviewed, CWE-918) names the exact sink — parse_sitemap's nested-sitemap loop calling self.scrape_all([loc.text], "xml") without the restrict_to_same_domain comparison applied to leaf url entries. Code archaeology: the nested loop was added in one commit, 7e79f8c (PR #3146, 2023-04-22, +7 lines), when the loader lived at langchain/document_loaders/sitemap.py; the parent 215dcc2d verifiably lacks it. The domain-restriction control arrived later (90e9ec6, 2023-10-17) but was wired only into the leaf-url loop, so the recursive loop has never enforced it — the flaw is exactly the first-write of the sink line. BIC = 7e79f8c (first-write, smallest surviving public object; its two patch-identical twins on side refs are the same PR's duplicates, not finer members). squash_decomposed=false: the later commits (split to langchain-community, max_depth cap) carried the unchanged sink rather than extending the flawed design. AI decision (BIC-only attribution): the BIC commit object is authored by a human (Johann-Peter Hartmann), squash-committed by GitHub, with only a self-co-author trailer; no AI markers — the Co-authored-by hit is the author's own identity, so verdict NOT_AI. The CVE-2024-2965 fix commits and any modern hardening elsewhere in the monorepo (SSRF utilities in langchain-core) are irrelevant to BIC attribution. Unpatched: the advisory names no fixed version, the monorepo has no post-split sitemap commits, and the sink is verbatim at langchain-community main HEAD; the only in-range remediation (max_depth, 9a877c7a) limits recursion depth but not destination, so the SSRF surface remains. Hence fix_sha=null/direct_fix_sha=null with the no-fix proof in evidence, reasoning, and remaining_gap.

potential_fix.approach: Validate sitemap URLs before recursion: restrict recursion to the same origin as the seed URL (or an explicit allowlist), cap recursion depth, and reject private/loopback resolved addresses.
potential_fix.rationale: Origin-scoped, depth-capped recursion with SSRF-safe address checks keeps SitemapLoader from being pointed at internal endpoints while preserving legitimate nested sitemaps.
